hypothesis: Raising EasyCache's threshold from 0.20 to 0.25, selected from round-8 accumulated-distance evidence, will convert one marginal recompute into a cache hit and place EasyCache inside the 28.0-28.5 second aggressive TeaCache/TaylorSeer band.

build.tests: 9/9 CPU tests passed; EasyCache calibration/hit behavior, ledger validation, dry-run, git diff, exact lease UUID, GPU-idle, and shared-lock availability preflights passed. The optional DeepGEMM warning remained benign.

run.signal_definition: EasyCache runtime-adaptive input-to-output transformation rate multiplied by current token-subsampled input change and normalized by previous output magnitude
run.reuse_payload: separate conditional and unconditional full-block-stack residual histories

validity.visual_note: The first/middle/last frames are coherent and retain identity, anatomy, forest structure, and flare progression without a gross artifact. Against matched aggressive TeaCache round 3 and TaylorSeer round 4, EasyCache is materially better than TaylorSeer; EasyCache and TeaCache are close and ambiguous on this single prompt. EasyCache keeps background and flare progression somewhat nearer dense, while both have pose/framing drift, so only a tentative Easy quality edge or tie is recorded.

decision.reason: Retain as the official matched aggressive EasyCache comparator: 28.4 s is within 0.351% of TeaCache round 3 and 1.429% of TaylorSeer round 4, the predicted 29-hit schedule was exact, and method, artifact, and lightweight visual validity pass. The one-prompt screen does not justify a decisive quality-superiority claim over TeaCache.
